From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: PolarisAI renewal — capacity runway & GPU recommendation

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for the time on Tuesday. I pulled together a short capacity runway based on the usage slices you shared and the Q3 spike pattern. Quick summary up front: current reserved pool = 8 A100s, baseline steady-state is ~1.6k QPS (avg tokens/minute ~1.1M), and our forecast models show a 2.3–2.7x token/QPS growth over the next 12 months given feature rollouts and marketing cadence.

Attached: polaris_qps_forecast.csv (hourly projection + percentiles).

Ask: ahead of the renewal call next week, can you confirm whether PolarisAI wants a firm committed capacity by product line (in which case we recommend a stepped reserved plan), or a blended committed + burst model? Our preliminary recommendation: 12 guaranteed GPUs in reserved pool with an 8-GPU burst buffer (auto-burst, billed at blended rate while in use). This supports p95 latency targets and gives runway for the expected 2.5x growth while keeping cost predictable.

Notes:
- Recommended guaranteed pool: 12x A100 equivalent (reserved)
- Recommended burst pool: 8x A100 equivalent (burst, best-effort)
- Baseline throughput target: support sustained 4k QPS peaks (5–10s windows)
- SLA ask: if Polaris needs strict p95 latency caps during peak windows we should discuss a higher guaranteed pool or a priority lane config.

Can we lock a 30-min slot Friday to walk the proposal and I’ll bring Marissa for pricing and Karthik for the ops plan?

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Quoted message:
> On Fri, 13 Nov 2026 at 10:12 AM Alex Cho <alex.cho@polaris.ai> wrote:
> > Thanks Marcus — this looks useful. A few quick items:

My thoughts:
- The forecast includes embeddings/batch traffic (we modeled a conservative +30% payload). The 2.5x figure is net of that.
- Cost delta (very rough): moving to 12 reserved from 8 increases committed monthly by ~52%. With the 8-GPU burst we estimate blended effective unit cost increase of ~28% net. I will run the definitive cost model but want to flag procurement pushback likely.
- Ops/SLA: propose a priority lane implementation that pins 25% of the reserved pool to latency-sensitive routes (chat completions) and leaves the rest elastic. That gives a deterministic p95 for customer-critical endpoints without requiring a 100% reserved uplift.

Recommendation for Friday: present a 2-phase renewal:
Phase 1 (0–3 months): 12x reserved (guaranteed), 8x burst; priority lane for chat endpoints (pin 3 GPUs)
Phase 2 (3–12 months): review with actual traffic; if p95 breaches or sustained 90th percentile token growth > 1.8x then convert 4 burst GPUs to reserved (bringing reserved to 16).

Attachments for Friday: redwood_proposal_v1.pdf (proposal summary) and cost_model_12mo.xlsx (breakdown).

- Marcus

- Guaranteed reserved pool: 12x A100-equivalent GPUs (committed)
- Burst buffer: 8x A100-equivalent GPUs (auto-burst, billed by usage)
